questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Mostly, it was the opportunity to visit a new university and a new city. Also, I wanted to get better at the language.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fine. I found most of the information on the host university's homepage.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I attended a meeting hosted by the receiving institution that was very helpful and where I could ask my questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: We were only two students at the institute, which made it a bit difficult to communicate with the other students. It would have been great if the institute had facilitated a meeting with other students as well.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was very lucky that I knew someone that I could rent a flat from.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Apparently, it should be pretty difficult to find housing. But maybe check Facebook pages or ask around in group chats.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I went into the homepage of the host institution and found the course selection. Then I followed the recieved information on how to register step by step.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I asked the coordinator at the institution as well as the teachers. So I actually just went to some of the classes, and then I could ask around.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Pretty successful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Go to the home page of the host institution and find the course selection. Dont be afraid to just meet up at the classes - both to check if the class is something for you but also to ask the teacher if you have any questions.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I only took MA level courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It reminded me a lot of how we do it at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. Ethnography Reloaded 
2. Anthropologische Differenzen 
3. Fundamentals for human-environment research

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Fundamentals for human-environment research was a very interesting class. It was interdisciplinary which made the discussions very interesting and I found that I was introduced to a lot of new perspectives, which is perfect for an exchange year.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not any acctually. Maybe the activities that I attended through the sports program that they had at the institution, but it was not that expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing was expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: University sport was very big at the institution.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I was attenending both football and volley, which was super fun and a good way to meet new people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: In general, museums, concerts, bars, etc. I really enjoyed staying in the city and really get to know the city that I was in.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy as it is very close to the country I am from.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: This can be rather difficult if you do not know the language, but maybe just try to by open and attending activities outside uni.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The many cultural activities in the city and the openness to other cultures.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Attend university sports if you enjoy doing some kind of sport!
2. Be prepared to meet new people and take the first initiative. 
3. Ask the teachers if you have any practical questions. They either know what to do or who to ask.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I bought a subscription for the cinemas in the city, which was very cheap (Cineville). I was there during winter, so it was just a very nice activity opportunity.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting local people. It was very helpful for me that I knew the language, and I was surprised by how open people were if I just tried to speak their language. Also, the cultural life is very vibrant, so remember to use it.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Maybe to get to know people in the beginning.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
